hypothesis: A Quaternary fault offsetting alluvium (or one lithology against itself) leaves a SUSTAINED topographic step: detrended elevation stays offset across the trace at both 200-300 m and 400-600 m apertures. Such a fault has no magnetic/gravity contrast, so the H19-5 potential-field worm skeleton behind R0 misses it, and a low scarp is easily missed by photo-era Qfaults mapping, while DEM-based expert mapping (the competition label source, DrivenData #306 p.967) traces exactly such steps. The min over apertures rejects channel walls/ridges, whose cross-line offset decays once the aperture exceeds their width (synthetic: 6 m step 5.4 m persistent vs channel 1.3 m).
mechanism: At fixed S=37,654, DTI rises when expected T gains outweigh denominator growth. Kept skeleton dots are chosen by exact marginal expected-DTI greedy (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, R=3px) under w=0.30+0.70*S on H19-5 support, so coverage-redundant parent dots are the donors. Far dots take the strongest aperture-persistent steps first (descending S, 2.8px spacing): the pre-build screen's identical 16,944-dot far set hit off-catalogue USGS SGMC bedrock faults at 0.071257 vs BREAKLINE-L 0.072325 while being 57% disjoint from BREAKLINE's far dots -- an independent evidence channel, not a reweighting.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Lake Lahontan wave-cut shoreline benches are sustained steps at all apertures; so are alluvial-fan segment boundaries, fluvial terrace edges, bedding-controlled cuestas and (without a coherence gate) rugged range-interior relief. Any of these concentrated in the far set would be pure false positives.

bootstrap.caveat: Conditional on fitted folds, catalogue labels and fixed budgets; not a leaderboard interval.
